Superusers and roles with the BYPASSRLS attribute always bypass the row security system when accessing a table.

retrieved_evidence.text: DROP POLICY removes the specified row-level security policy from a table. Dropping the last policy of a table does not disable row security; the default-deny policy still applies while row security is enabled.

CREATE POLICY defines a new row-level security policy for a table. The policy name must be unique per table, and the policy applies to the roles named in its TO clause, or to PUBLIC if no roles are named.
Policies can be specified for SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or ALL commands. A policy for ALL applies to every command type.

When row security is enabled on a table (with ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY), all normal access to the table for selecting rows or modifying rows must be allowed by a row security policy. If no policy exists for the table, a default-deny policy is used, so that no rows are visible or updatable.
The table's owner is typically not subject to row security policies, though a table owner can choose to be subject to row security with ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
